title: General polynomial-chart model and refinement comparison for coherent relative duality
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated, flat, locally finitely presented morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $S$ locally Noetherian (covered by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]). There exists a relative dualizing pair $(D_f,\xi_f)$: $D_f\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] is pseudo-coherent (locally represented by a bounded-above complex of finite-rank free modules) and has finite Tor amplitude over $S$ (derived tensoring with any $\mathcal O_S$-module has cohomology in a fixed finite interval locally on $X$); writing $\Delta:X\hookrightarrow X\times_SX$ and $\operatorname{pr}_1:X\times_SX\to X$, the map $\xi_f:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to L\operatorname{pr}_1^*D_f$ induces an isomorphism $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\simeq R\mathcal Hom(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,L\operatorname{pr}_1^*D_f)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Here a derived pullback is computed using flat resolutions before tensoring. On an affine-local presentation $U\xrightarrow{i}P\to S$, with $P$ an open of $\mathbf A^n_S$ and $i$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], the underlying relative dualizing object is represented by $R\mathcal Hom_P(i_*\mathcal O_U,\Omega^n_{P/S}[n])$, with its natural $\mathcal O_U$-module structure. Here $\Omega^n$ is the $n$th exterior power [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra] of the sheaf of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. The comparisons of these models under different polynomial presentations are the canonical comparisons obtained from restriction and polynomial refinements, compatible with composition. In a one-variable refinement $Q=A[t]\twoheadrightarrow A$, $t\mapsto a$, the comparison is normalized by the two-term resolution $[Q\xrightarrow{t-a}Q]$ and the contraction $\operatorname{Hom}_{A}( (t-a)/(t-a)^2,A)\otimes_A A\,d(t-a)\to A$ sending the dual of $t-a$ tensored with $d(t-a)$ to $1$. Iterated refinements use the corresponding ordered Koszul contraction and the usual cohomological tensor signs. No complete-intersection, constant-dimension, or invertibility hypothesis on $D_f$ is assumed.
